passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David was king of Israel.
Nathan was a prophet.
Nathan came to David.
Nathan came after David committed adultery with Bathsheba.
This psalm is for the choirmaster.

passages.text: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David was king of Israel.
David sinned with Bathsheba.
Nathan the prophet came to David after this sin.
David prayed to God.
David said, “God, have mercy on me.”
God is loving and faithful.
God is full of compassion.
David asked God to show His mercy.
David asked God to erase his sins.
David asked God to remove his transgressions because of God’s great compassion.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ בְּֽבוֹא־ אֵ֭לָיו נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֝֗א אֶל־ בַּת־ שָֽׁבַע׃ חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי׃

passages.text: Wash me clean of my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm after Nathan the prophet confronted him about his adultery with Bathsheba.
David speaks to God.
David says, "Wash me clean of my iniquity."
David says, "Cleanse me from my sin."

passages.text: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
passages.sermon: David is speaking to God.\r\nDavid knows his transgressions.\r\nDavid sees his sin before him at all times.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ פְ֭שָׁעַי אֲנִ֣י אֵדָ֑ע וְחַטָּאתִ֖י נֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David confesses his sin.
David says he sinned against God alone.
David says he did what is evil in God’s sight.
David wants God to be shown as right when God speaks.
David wants God to be blameless when God judges.
passages.original: לְךָ֤ לְבַדְּךָ֨׀ חָטָאתִי֮ וְהָרַ֥ע בְּעֵינֶ֗יךָ עָ֫שִׂ֥יתִי לְ֭מַעַן תִּצְדַּ֥ק בְּדָבְרֶ֗ךָ תִּזְכֶּ֥ה בְשָׁפְטֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Surely I was brought forth in iniquity; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
David confesses his sin.
David says, “I was brought forth in iniquity.”
David means he was born into sin.
David says, “I was sinful when my mother conceived me.”
David means he had a sinful nature from the beginning.
David admits he has always needed God’s mercy.
passages.original: הֵן־ בְּעָו֥וֹן חוֹלָ֑לְתִּי וּ֝בְחֵ֗טְא יֶֽחֱמַ֥תְנִי אִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
passages.sermon:
God desires truth.
God wants truth deep inside a person.
God teaches wisdom.
God gives wisdom in the secret, hidden places of the heart.
passages.original: הֵן־ אֱ֭מֶת חָפַ֣צְתָּ בַטֻּח֑וֹת וּ֝בְסָתֻ֗ם חָכְמָ֥ה תוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
passages.sermon:
God, you can purify me.
You can use hyssop to make me clean.
If you wash me, I will be clean.
If you wash me, I will be whiter than snow.
passages.original: תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי בְאֵז֣וֹב וְאֶטְהָ֑ר תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי וּמִשֶּׁ֥לֶג אַלְבִּֽין׃

passages.text: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.
passages.sermon:
God, you have power over my life.
You can give me joy.
You can give me gladness.
Let me hear joy.
Let me hear gladness.
You have crushed my bones.
Let my crushed bones rejoice.
passages.original: תַּ֭שְׁמִיעֵנִי שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה תָּ֝גֵ֗לְנָה עֲצָמ֥וֹת דִּכִּֽיתָ׃

passages.text: Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities.
passages.sermon:
God, you see all things.
I have sinned.
I have done wrong.
Turn your face away from my sins.
Remove all my iniquities.
Erase every wrong I have done.
passages.original: הַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵחֲטָאָ֑י וְֽכָל־ עֲוֺ֖נֹתַ֣י מְחֵֽה׃

passages.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
passages.sermon:
God, you are holy and powerful.
I ask you to create a clean heart in me.
I want a heart that is pure and free from sin.
Renew a right spirit within me.
Give me a spirit that is faithful and steadfast.
Place this spirit deep inside me.
passages.original: לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא־ לִ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ נָ֝כ֗וֹן חַדֵּ֥שׁ בְּקִרְבִּֽי׃

passages.text: Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me.
passages.sermon:
God, You are holy.
You are present with Your people.
Do not cast me away from Your presence.
Do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥נִי מִלְּפָנֶ֑יךָ וְר֥וּחַ קָ֝דְשְׁךָ֗ אַל־ תִּקַּ֥ח מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
passages.sermon:
God, you save me.
You give salvation.
I once had joy because of your salvation.
Now I have lost that joy.
Please give me back the joy that comes from your salvation.
Give me a spirit that is willing to obey you.
Keep me strong with this willing spirit.
passages.original: הָשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֭י שְׂשׂ֣וֹן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וְר֖וּחַ נְדִיבָ֣ה תִסְמְכֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David has sinned.
David asks God for forgiveness.
David promises to act after God forgives him.
David says, “I will teach transgressors Your ways.”
Transgressors are people who break God’s laws.
David will show them how God wants people to live.
David says, “Sinners will return to You.”
Sinners are people who have turned away from God.
David believes they will come back to God.
passages.original: אֲלַמְּדָ֣ה פֹשְׁעִ֣ים דְּרָכֶ֑יךָ וְ֝חַטָּאִ֗ים אֵלֶ֥יךָ יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃

passages.text: Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness.
passages.sermon:
God is the God who saves me.
I have guilt because of bloodshed.
God, deliver me from this guilt.
If You save me, I will praise You.
My tongue will sing about Your righteousness.
passages.original: הַצִּ֘ילֵ֤נִי מִדָּמִ֨ים׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י תְּשׁוּעָתִ֑י תְּרַנֵּ֥ן לְ֝שׁוֹנִ֗י צִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.
passages.sermon:
O Lord, you are the one I address.
You have power to open my lips.
Open my lips, Lord.
Then my mouth will declare your praise.
I will speak your praise with my mouth.
passages.original: אֲ֭דֹנָי שְׂפָתַ֣י תִּפְתָּ֑ח וּ֝פִ֗י יַגִּ֥יד תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
passages.sermon:
God does not delight in sacrifice.
God does not take pleasure in burnt offerings.
If God wanted sacrifice, I would bring it.
But God does not desire these offerings.
passages.original: כִּ֤י׀ לֹא־ תַחְפֹּ֣ץ זֶ֣בַח וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה ע֝וֹלָ֗ה לֹ֣א תִרְצֶֽה׃

passages.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm after Doeg the Edomite told Saul about him.
David speaks to God.
God values certain sacrifices.
God accepts a broken spirit.
God does not reject a broken heart.
God does not despise a contrite heart.
passages.original: זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֪וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב־ נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְנִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה׃

passages.text: In Your good pleasure, cause Zion to prosper; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
God, You have good pleasure.
You can bless Zion.
Please make Zion prosper.
You can build up Jerusalem.
Please build the walls of Jerusalem.
passages.original: הֵיטִ֣יבָה בִ֭רְצוֹנְךָ אֶת־ צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar.
passages.sermon: God will delight in righteous sacrifices.\r\nGod will accept whole burnt offerings.\r\nPeople will offer bulls on God's altar.
passages.original: אָ֤ז תַּחְפֹּ֣ץ זִבְחֵי־ צֶ֭דֶק עוֹלָ֣ה וְכָלִ֑יל אָ֤ז יַעֲל֖וּ עַל־ מִזְבַּחֲךָ֣ פָרִֽים׃
